reviews.title: Great for a Mac
reviews.comment: As a Desktop Mac user, it is hard to find a decent wired backlit mechanical keyboard at a good price. While all USB keyboards a compatible with a Mac, that is not the same thing as having a Mac keyboard layout. Being less expensive than many of the alternatives I found, I decided to give this one a try. I am very pleased with it. It has a pair of switches on the underside. One to switch between 2.4GHz, Bluetooth and off. And another, that is for Mac or Windows configuration. Switched it to Mac and left wireless turned off. Plugged it into my KVM and the was greeted by the macOS keyboard setup wizard. Afterwards, it worked like any normal Mac specific keyboard. Having the Command key next to the space bar for shortcuts like Copy&Paste was a must. No problem there. The extra media keys work great as well. However, they only light up when pressed. As a non-gamer, I did not think I would have much use for the Macro keys. But, I was wrong and set the first one up to do screen captures of the current window. I am very used to the brown switches on my old keyboard. This one has hot swap-able Red Linear switches. It will take a little while to get accustomed to their feel. But, they are comfortable, work great and are quieter. Out of the box, the RGB backlights were setup to perform a Las Vegas Christmas light show. While neat, not something I actually would want to have on a regular basis. Thankfully, it has different lighting modes and color schemes. I set mine to an unchanging near white and I'm happy. It is also possible to assigned each key one of 7 colors. I was able to do all of the things I mentioned above without ever setting up wireless or installing any software. Overall, it seems to be a great keyboard. Did I mention it even has the old school Num Lock, Caps Lock and Scroll Lock LEDs. Plus, it can live as a strictly USB keyboard.
reviews.author: JJ

reviews.title: Great value, has all I want
reviews.comment: Nice keyboard.  Has all the features needed.  Wireless or wired.  Nice font on the keys that has good RGB passthru and there isn't too much RGB color bleed between the keys.  Volume wheel is always a must for me and this one is metal with a nice click feel to it.  You can also change the function of the wheel to change brightness etc.  I installed the software and it works well but almost everything can be controlled without software via keyboard inputs.  Once you configure the software, your choices can be saved to the board and you can remove the software if you choose.  You can easily change the keycaps and switches but I'm liking these pretty well so far.  Red linear, good sound and actuation is just perfect for me so far.

reviews.title: Great but with a great flaw that may make the entire keyboard useless.
reviews.comment:
The feeling and sound and built of the keyboard are great for the price, as Redragon usually is.
But this keyboard has an annoying issue where (since it has a button to switch between MAC and Windows) it changes randomly to MAC layout. I have to use the button to actually place it on mac position and back to windows.
Right now it doesn't even let me play my game, since when on MAC, the ALT key becomes Windows key, so every time I need to use the ALT, it opens the start menu.
F keys also stop working as they should be, F2 becomes brightness level, etc.... If this keeps happening more frequently (it comes and goes) the keyboard becomes trash, since you can't type or game if keys suddenly change what they do.
reviews.author: Ale. A

reviews.title: Mine was clearly pre-owned even though I paid full price. Make sure its put together well.
reviews.comment:
I paid the full $69 for this (and now its on discount for $64), and it came without a box or manual, just wrapped in plastic, as though it was used. The adhesive on the plastic was so sticky it wouldn't come off the keyboard without a lot of effort. I still haven't gotten it all off.
The keys had something sprayed on them. I can only imagine what.
It came with several replacement switches, one of which was missing.
The top panel with the scroll wheel is not securely attached at all.
I think I got a lemon, or some warehouse mishap. I'm not sure what, but I'm not happy about it.
Putting all of that aside, i really like the features/functionality of the keyboard. It has a toggle to switch between mac/windows. Pairs with multiple devices via bluetooth. It's pretty slick, but not the cheapest option.
